skill.name: security-audit
skill.description: Security audit guidance for reviewing code, architecture, infrastructure, supply chain, cryptography, smart contracts, and ZK systems.

content.user_title: Audit Security Risks with Structured Checklists
content.value_statement: Security reviews can miss important controls when teams rely on ad hoc questions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured audits across application, infrastructure, supply chain, cryptography, smart contract, and ZK domains.
actual_capabilities: Guides threat modeling with STRIDE categories and trust-boundary questions.
Reviews identity, access control, secrets, cryptography, injection, infrastructure, and CI/CD controls.
Provides domain checklists for web applications, supply chain security, cryptography, smart contracts, and ZK circuits.
Maps review concerns to frameworks such as NIST SSDF, OWASP ASVS, SLSA, OpenSSF Scorecard, and MITRE ATT&CK.
Produces structured findings with severity, category, location, impact, recommendation, and references.
limitations: It provides review guidance and does not automatically scan repositories or run security tools.
It cannot replace a formal penetration test or specialist audit for high-risk systems.
Findings depend on the code, architecture details, and context supplied by the user.
It does not verify fixes unless the user separately asks for implementation or testing work.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request for security impact
use_cases.description: Assess authentication, authorization, input handling, secrets, logging, and dependency changes before merge.

use_cases.title: Prepare a product threat model
use_cases.description: Identify assets, trust boundaries, abuse cases, and missing controls before a launch or architecture review.

use_cases.title: Check specialized cryptographic or blockchain components
use_cases.description: Use focused checklists for cryptography, smart contracts, supply chain integrity, and ZK circuit soundness.

prompt_templates.title: Basic security review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-audit skill to review this change for authentication, authorization, input validation, secrets, and logging risks. Return prioritized findings with clear fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Threat model a feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning a new feature before implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-audit skill to threat model this feature. Identify assets, trust boundaries, STRIDE risks, abuse cases, required controls, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Supply chain assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-audit skill to assess our supply chain posture. Focus on dependency pinning, CI/CD permissions, provenance, release signing, vulnerability response, and runner isolation.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced domain audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Reviewing cryptography, smart contracts, or ZK circuits
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-audit skill for a deep audit of this high-risk component. Apply the relevant domain checklist, state assumptions, identify exploitable failure modes, and propose concrete remediations.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that changes session handling and adds a new admin endpoint.
output: High severity finding for missing resource-level authorization on the admin endpoint.
Medium severity finding for sessions not rotating after privilege changes.
Recommendations for server-side authorization checks, session regeneration, and audit logging.

output_examples.input: Threat model a file upload service before launch.
output: Assets and trust boundaries for user files, storage, scanning, and delivery paths.
Abuse cases covering malware upload, content-type bypass, path traversal, and stored XSS.
Controls for magic-byte validation, size limits, non-executable storage, randomized names, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Assess a repository for supply chain security readiness.
output: Checklist results for dependency pinning, vulnerability scanning, branch protection, signed releases, and provenance.
Priority gaps with suggested owners and remediation order.
Follow-up verification steps for CI permissions and release artifact integrity.

best_practices: Provide architecture diagrams, changed files, threat assumptions, and deployment context before asking for review.
Ask for severity, exploit scenario, impact, and remediation for each finding.
Use the domain-specific checklist that matches the reviewed system, then verify fixes separately.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the output as a complete penetration test without manual validation.
Do not ask for exploit instructions against systems you do not own or have permission to test.
Do not merge high-risk changes based only on checklist completion without testing the controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help review?
faq.answer: It helps review code, architecture, infrastructure, CI/CD, dependencies, cryptography, smart contracts, and ZK circuits for security risks.

faq.question: Does it run automated scanners?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured guidance and review criteria. You can separately ask Claude Code to run available project tools.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it reference?
faq.answer: It references NIST CSF, CIS Controls, NIST SSDF, OWASP ASVS, OWASP Top 10, MITRE ATT&CK, SLSA, and OpenSSF Scorecard.

faq.question: Can it review blockchain systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for smart contracts, protocol risks, oracle and bridge assumptions, key custody, and ZK circuit checks.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated environments?
faq.answer: It can support internal reviews, but formal compliance or assurance work still needs qualified human review and evidence collection.

faq.question: How should I use the findings?
faq.answer: Treat them as prioritized review output. Validate each finding, implement the remediation, and retest the affected control.
